criteria.criterion: athena-data records.rs defines athena.candidate/2 with base_fingerprint and optional previous_job, registered in AnyRecord and the schema-name table; athena.candidate/1 still parses.
criteria.evidence: From the diff of records.rs: `Candidate` gains `base_fingerprint: Option<String>` and `previous_job: Option<JobId>`, both `serde(default, skip_serializing_if)`. A new `AnyRecord::Candidate2` variant is renamed `athena.candidate/2` and appears in `schema()` and in the path table. `parse` refuses a /1 that carries either new field and a /2 that has no base_fingerprint. The test candidate_1_still_parses_and_keeps_its_shape passes.

criteria.criterion: docs/records.md documents athena.candidate/2 and its two new fields.
criteria.evidence: From the diff: docs/records.md adds a table row for `athena.candidate/2` that describes base_fingerprint (required) and previous_job (optional, left out when there is none, derived by the core). The layout line now names /2 and says older jobs keep /1.

criteria.criterion: athena-core run.rs writes /2 candidates with base_fingerprint computed from the base commit and previous_job set to the latest landed job in the base's history (absent if none).
criteria.evidence: From the diff: run.rs sets `base_fingerprint: Some(fingerprint(&self.git, &p, &p)?)`, which is the base tree under the base's own rules (the signature in attrs.rs is fingerprint(git, treeish, rules_commit)). It sets `previous_job` from the new `chain::latest_landed_job(&self.git, &p)`, which walks the base's history newest first and returns the first commit that adds a landed outcome. The record is written as `AnyRecord::Candidate2`.

criteria.criterion: store.rs and every other AnyRecord::Candidate consumer (scoring, athena-score, athena-git snapshot, gate jobs.rs) compile and handle /2 without changing gate landing, jobs or history rules.
criteria.evidence: Grep for AnyRecord::Candidate finds only records.rs, store.rs (two match arms extended), gate jobs.rs (one arm extended), landing_tests.rs and lifecycle.rs. scoring.rs, athena-score and snapshot.rs never match the variant (they use the shared Candidate struct or an unrelated SnapshotRepo enum), so they need no change. The gate edit only adds `| Candidate2(c)` to the arm that stores the record, so no rule changes. clippy passed.

criteria.criterion: Tests cover /2 round-trip, /1 still parsing, and the core writing base_fingerprint and previous_job (including previous_job absent when no job has landed).
criteria.evidence: These tests pass: records::candidate_2_round_trips_with_and_without_a_previous_job, candidate_1_still_parses_and_keeps_its_shape, candidate_versions_keep_to_their_fields, chain::no_landed_job_means_no_previous_job, and chain::the_latest_landed_job_is_named_and_hand_changes_are_skipped. The lifecycle test a_request_lands_a_traceable_commit checks that the core wrote base_fingerprint equal to the base's fingerprint and that previous_job is None.

criteria.evidence: The diff shows no change to invariant.rs or records/. The design doc status still reads 'proposed (D69)' and gains a progress note saying the gate rule is not built. The CHANGELOG entry says the gate still refuses a commit that lands more than one job.

summary: The change passes. It adds `athena.candidate/2` as a second tagged variant over the shared `Candidate` type, with an optional `base_fingerprint` and `previous_job`. Parsing makes sure each field appears only under the right version: /1 refuses both fields and /2 requires base_fingerprint. The core now writes /2. It computes base_fingerprint from the base commit under the base's own rules, and takes previous_job from a new `chain::latest_landed_job`, which walks the base's history and skips hand changes. The only consumers that match the record variant (store.rs and gate jobs.rs) now accept /2 without any rule change. invariant.rs and records/ are untouched. The design doc stays 'proposed', with a progress note, and the CHANGELOG says the gate rule comes next. Tests cover the /2 round-trip, /1 still parsing, version-field checks, the history walk, and the core writing base_fingerprint and leaving previous_job absent. I ran cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test, and all passed. One minor gap: no end-to-end test shows the core writing a previous_job that is set; that case is tested only in the unit tests for the history walk.
